title.en: Tuesday Homework: Waves, Sound and Hearing (B1 to B3)
title.zh: 星期二作业：波、声音和听觉（B1 到 B3）

subtitle.en: 12 questions, try as often as you like

intro.en: Read Main Book B1 to B3 first. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 先读主课本 B1 到 B3。可以做很多次。

questions.q: A wave transfers ___ from one place to another.

why.en: A wave carries ENERGY from one place to another, but the particles only vibrate and stay where they are. (A duck on a wave bobs up and down; it does not travel with the wave.)
why.zh: 波把能量从一个地方传到另一个地方，但粒子只是振动，留在原地。（水面上的鸭子只是上下浮动，不会跟着波走。）

particles.en: The particles only vibrate about one spot. They do not travel along with the wave.
particles.zh: 粒子只在一个位置附近振动，不会跟着波一起走。

water.en: In a water wave the water moves up and down, but it does not travel across the ocean. Energy does.
water.zh: 水波里的水只是上下动，不会横穿大海。传过去的是能量。

air.en: In sound, air particles vibrate back and forth but stay in place. Only the energy moves along.
air.zh: 声音里的空气粒子前后振动但留在原地，只有能量往前传。

questions.qzh: 波把 ___ 从一个地方传到另一个地方。

questions.q: In a transverse wave, the vibrations are ___ to the direction of travel.

why.en: Perpendicular means at 90° (a right angle). In a transverse wave the particles move up and down while the wave travels forward.
why.zh: perpendicular 是“垂直的”（90°）。横波的粒子上下振动，而波往前传。

parallel.en: Parallel (same direction) describes a LONGITUDINAL wave.

opposite.en: Opposite would be backwards along the line, which is still parallel, not at 90°.
opposite.zh: 相反是沿着直线往回，还是平行，不是 90°。

unrelated.en: The vibration direction is always related to the travel direction: 90° for transverse, parallel for longitudinal.
unrelated.zh: 振动方向和传播方向一定有关系：横波是 90°，纵波是平行。

questions.qzh: 横波的振动方向和传播方向是 ___ 的。

questions.q: Sound is a ___ wave.

why.en: In sound, the particles vibrate backwards and forwards ALONG the direction the wave travels (compressions and rarefactions). Vibrations parallel to the direction of travel make a longitudinal wave.
why.zh: 声音里，粒子沿着波传播的方向前后振动（疏部和密部）。振动方向和传播方向平行的是纵波。

transverse.en: In a transverse wave (light, water ripples), particles move UP and DOWN, at right angles to the direction of travel. Sound particles move back and forth along it.
transverse.zh: 横波（光、水波）的粒子上下振动，和传播方向垂直。声音的粒子是沿着方向前后振动。

electromagnetic.en: Electromagnetic waves (light, radio) can travel through a vacuum. Sound cannot, because it needs particles.
electromagnetic.zh: 电磁波（光、无线电）能在真空中传播。声音不能，因为它需要粒子。

light.en: Light is a transverse, electromagnetic wave, a different kind from sound.
light.zh: 光是横波、电磁波，和声音不是一类。

questions.qzh: 声音是一种 ___ 波。

questions.q: In a longitudinal wave, a region where particles are close together is a...

why.en: In a longitudinal wave the particles bunch up in some places and spread out in others. Where they are squashed CLOSE together is a compression (compress = squeeze).
why.zh: 纵波里粒子有的地方挤在一起，有的地方散开。挤在一起的地方叫密部（compress = 压缩）。

rarefaction.en: A rarefaction is where particles are SPREAD apart, the opposite.
rarefaction.zh: 疏部是粒子散开的地方，正相反。

crest.en: Crests are the tops of TRANSVERSE waves, not part of a longitudinal wave.
crest.zh: 波峰是横波的最高点，不属于纵波。

trough.en: Troughs are the bottoms of TRANSVERSE waves.

questions.qzh: 在纵波里，粒子挤在一起的地方叫……

questions.q: Amplitude is measured from the ___ to the crest.

why.en: Amplitude is the biggest distance a point moves away from its rest (middle) position, so measure from the rest line up to the crest.
why.zh: 振幅是一个点离开平衡（中间）位置的最大距离，所以从平衡线量到波峰。

next crest.en: Crest to next crest is the WAVELENGTH.
next crest.zh: 波峰到下一个波峰是波长。

trough.en: Trough to crest is TWICE the amplitude.
trough.zh: 波谷到波峰是振幅的两倍。

source.en: The source is where the wave started, not a point on the wave.
source.zh: 波源是波开始的地方，不是波上的点。

questions.qzh: 振幅是从 ___ 量到波峰。

questions.q: 10 complete waves pass a point in 2 seconds. What is the frequency?

why.en: Frequency = number of waves ÷ time. 10 ÷ 2 = 5 waves per second = 5 Hz.
why.zh: 频率 = 波数 ÷ 时间。10 ÷ 2 = 每秒 5 个波 = 5 Hz。

20 Hz.en: 20 is 10 × 2: it multiplied by the time. Frequency is per second, so divide.
20 Hz.zh: 20 是 10 × 2，乘了时间。频率是每秒多少，要除。

questions.qzh: 2 秒内有 10 个完整的波经过一个点。频率是多少？

questions.q: Why can sound NOT travel through a vacuum?
options: there are no particles to vibrate

why.en: Sound is a vibration passed from particle to particle. A vacuum has NO particles, so there is nothing to pass the vibration on.
why.zh: 声音是粒子一个传一个的振动。真空里没有粒子，所以没有东西能传递振动。

it is too cold.en: Temperature is not the reason. Even a hot vacuum carries no sound, because there are no particles.
it is too cold.zh: 原因不是温度。就算是热的真空也传不了声音，因为没有粒子。

light blocks it.en: Light does not block sound. Light and sound pass through each other.
light blocks it.zh: 光不会挡住声音，光和声音可以互相穿过。

the frequency is too high.en: No frequency of sound can cross a vacuum, high or low.
the frequency is too high.zh: 不管频率高低，声音都不能穿过真空。

questions.qzh: 为什么声音不能在真空中传播？

questions.q: A higher frequency gives a...

why.en: Pitch depends on frequency: more vibrations each second = a higher note.
why.zh: 音调取决于频率：每秒振动越多，音越高。

louder sound.en: Loudness depends on AMPLITUDE, not frequency.
louder sound.zh: 响度取决于振幅，不是频率。

quieter sound.en: Frequency does not change loudness; amplitude does.
quieter sound.zh: 频率不改变响度，振幅才会。

lower pitch.en: Higher frequency gives a HIGHER pitch, not lower.
lower pitch.zh: 频率越高，音调越高，不是越低。

questions.qzh: 频率越高，……

questions.q: A bigger amplitude gives a...

why.en: Loudness depends on amplitude: bigger vibrations carry more energy, so the sound is louder.
why.zh: 响度取决于振幅：振动越大能量越多，声音越响。

higher pitch.en: Pitch depends on FREQUENCY, not amplitude.
higher pitch.zh: 音调取决于频率，不是振幅。

lower pitch.en: Amplitude does not change the pitch at all.
lower pitch.zh: 振幅完全不会改变音调。

faster sound.en: The speed of sound depends on the medium, not on amplitude.
faster sound.zh: 声速取决于介质，不是振幅。

questions.qzh: 振幅越大，……

questions.q: A dog whistle at 25,000 Hz is...

why.en: Humans hear about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. 25,000 Hz is ABOVE that, and sound above our hearing is ultrasound (ultra = beyond).
why.zh: 人能听到约 20 Hz 到 20,000 Hz。25,000 Hz 高于这个范围，高于人类听力的是超声波（ultra = 超过）。

infrasound.en: Infrasound is BELOW 20 Hz. 25,000 Hz is very high.
infrasound.zh: 次声波低于 20 Hz。25,000 Hz 很高。

in the human audible range.en: Humans hear only up to about 20,000 Hz, so 25,000 Hz is too high for us.
in the human audible range.zh: 人只能听到约 20,000 Hz，25,000 Hz 对我们来说太高了。

an echo.en: An echo is a reflected sound, at any frequency. The question is about how high it is.
an echo.zh: 回声是反射的声音，什么频率都可能。题目问的是有多高。

questions.qzh: 25,000 Hz 的狗哨是……

questions.q: Which part of the ear turns vibrations into electrical signals?

why.en: The cochlea converts vibrations into electrical signals.
why.zh: 耳蜗把振动变成电信号。

eardrum.en: The eardrum VIBRATES when sound hits it, but it does not make electrical signals.
eardrum.zh: 鼓膜被声音打到会振动，但不会产生电信号。

pinna.en: The pinna is the outer ear flap. It only collects sound.
pinna.zh: 耳廓是外耳，只负责收集声音。

ossicles.en: The ossicles are tiny bones that pass on and AMPLIFY the vibration. The cochlea changes it into signals.
ossicles.zh: 听小骨是把振动传过去并放大的小骨头。耳蜗才把它变成信号。

questions.qzh: 耳朵的哪个部分把振动变成电信号？

questions.q: Which is the correct order as sound travels into the ear?
options: pinna, auditory canal, eardrum, ossicles, cochlea, auditory nerve
eardrum, pinna, cochlea, ossicles, auditory canal, auditory nerve
pinna, eardrum, auditory canal, cochlea, ossicles, auditory nerve
auditory nerve, cochlea, ossicles, eardrum, auditory canal, pinna

why.en: Collect, carry, vibrate, amplify, convert, send to the brain.
why.zh: 收集、传送、振动、放大、转换、送到大脑。

eardrum, pinna, cochlea, ossicles, audit.en: Sound enters at the PINNA first, then travels down the canal to the eardrum.
eardrum, pinna, cochlea, ossicles, audit.zh: 声音先进入耳廓，再沿耳道到鼓膜。

pinna, eardrum, auditory canal, cochlea,.en: The canal comes BEFORE the eardrum (it leads to it), and the ossicles come before the cochlea.
pinna, eardrum, auditory canal, cochlea,.zh: 耳道在鼓膜前面（通向鼓膜），听小骨在耳蜗前面。

auditory nerve, cochlea, ossicles, eardr.en: This is the right list but backwards, from the brain outwards.
auditory nerve, cochlea, ossicles, eardr.zh: 顺序对，但反过来了，是从大脑往外。

questions.qzh: 声音进入耳朵的正确顺序是哪个？

ozh.pinna, auditory canal, eardrum, ossicles: 耳廓、耳道、鼓膜、听小骨、耳蜗、听神经
ozh.eardrum, pinna, cochlea, ossicles, audit: 鼓膜、耳廓、耳蜗、听小骨、耳道、听神经
ozh.pinna, eardrum, auditory canal, cochlea,: 耳廓、鼓膜、耳道、耳蜗、听小骨、听神经
ozh.auditory nerve, cochlea, ossicles, eardr: 听神经、耳蜗、听小骨、鼓膜、耳道、耳廓

canNow.zh: 我现在能解释波、声音以及我们怎样听到声音。

cards.back: A low-frequency electromagnetic wave used for radio and television communication.
cards.zhBack: 低频电磁波，用于广播和电视通信。

cards.back: An electromagnetic wave used in cooking, radar and satellite communication.
cards.zhBack: 用于烹饪、雷达和卫星通信的电磁波。

cards.back: Electromagnetic radiation associated with heat, used in thermal imaging and remote controls.
cards.zhBack: 和热有关的电磁辐射，用于热成像和遥控器。

cards.back: The part of the electromagnetic spectrum that can be detected by the human eye.
cards.zhBack: 电磁波谱中人眼能看见的部分。

cards.back: Electromagnetic radiation with a higher frequency than visible light, which can cause sunburn and damage skin cells.
cards.zhBack: 频率比可见光高的电磁辐射，会晒伤皮肤、伤害皮肤细胞。

cards.back: High-frequency electromagnetic radiation that can pass through soft tissue and is used to produce medical images.
cards.zhBack: 高频电磁辐射，能穿过软组织，用来拍医学影像。

cards.back: Very high-frequency electromagnetic radiation that can be produced by radioactive materials and used in cancer treatment.
cards.zhBack: 频率非常高的电磁辐射，可由放射性物质产生，用于治疗癌症。

cards.back: Radiation with enough energy to remove electrons from atoms, potentially damaging cells and DNA.
cards.zhBack: 能量大到能把电子从原子中打出来的辐射，可能伤害细胞和 DNA。

cards.back: Radio, microwave, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma: low frequency to high frequency.
cards.zhBack: 无线电波、微波、红外线、可见光、紫外线、X 射线、伽马射线：从低频到高频。

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave is a ___ wave that can travel through a vacuum.

why.en: School definition: a transverse wave that can travel through a vacuum without needing a medium.
why.zh: 学校定义：一种横波，不需要介质，能在真空中传播。

longitudinal.en: Longitudinal waves (like sound) need particles, so they cannot cross a vacuum. EM waves are transverse.
longitudinal.zh: 纵波（像声音）需要粒子，不能穿过真空。电磁波是横波。

sound.en: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum at all.
sound.zh: 声音根本不能在真空中传播。

water.en: Water waves need water to travel in.

questions.qzh: 电磁波是一种能在真空中传播的 ___ 波。

questions.q: Which can travel through a vacuum?

why.en: Light is an EM wave. Sound needs a medium (B1).
why.zh: 光是电磁波。声音需要介质（B1）。

sound.en: Sound needs particles (a medium). A vacuum has none.
sound.zh: 声音需要粒子（介质），真空里没有。

a water wave.en: A water wave is a disturbance OF water, so it needs water.
a water wave.zh: 水波是水的扰动，需要水。

a wave on a slinky.en: A slinky wave travels through the slinky's coils; it needs the slinky.
a wave on a slinky.zh: 弹簧上的波要靠弹簧的圈传播，需要弹簧。

questions.qzh: 哪个能在真空中传播？

questions.q: Which EM wave has the LOWEST frequency?

why.en: EM spectrum from lowest to highest frequency: Radio, Microwave, Infrared, Visible, Ultraviolet, X-ray, Gamma. Radio waves are at the LOW end (and have the longest wavelength).
why.zh: 电磁波谱从低频到高频：无线电波、微波、红外线、可见光、紫外线、X 光、伽马射线。无线电波在低频端（波长最长）。

gamma ray.en: Gamma rays are at the HIGHEST frequency end.
gamma ray.zh: 伽马射线在最高频的一端。

X-ray.en: X-rays are very high frequency, second only to gamma.
X-ray.zh: X 光频率很高，仅次于伽马射线。

ultraviolet.en: Ultraviolet is higher than visible light, near the top end.
ultraviolet.zh: 紫外线比可见光高，接近高频端。

questions.qzh: 哪种电磁波的频率最低？

questions.q: Which EM wave has the HIGHEST frequency?

why.en: EM spectrum from low to high frequency: Radio, Microwave, Infrared, Visible, Ultraviolet, X-ray, Gamma. Gamma is at the TOP end (highest frequency, most energy).
why.zh: 电磁波谱从低频到高频：无线电波、微波、红外线、可见光、紫外线、X 光、伽马射线。伽马射线在最高端（频率最高、能量最大）。

radio wave.en: Radio waves are at the LOWEST frequency end.
radio wave.zh: 无线电波在最低频的一端。

microwave.en: Microwaves are low frequency, second from the bottom.

infrared.en: Infrared is below visible light, in the lower half.
infrared.zh: 红外线在可见光下面，在低频那一半。

questions.qzh: 哪种电磁波的频率最高？

questions.q: Which is the correct order from low to high frequency?
options: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma
gamma, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwave, radio
radio, infrared, microwave, visible, X-ray, ultraviolet, gamma
microwave, radio, visible, infrared, ultraviolet, gamma, X-ray

why.en: Low to high frequency: Radio, Microwave, Infrared, Visible, Ultraviolet, X-ray, Gamma. Mnemonic: Rabbits Mate In Very Unusual eXpensive Gardens.
why.zh: 低频到高频：无线电波、微波、红外线、可见光、紫外线、X 光、伽马射线。记法：Rabbits Mate In Very Unusual eXpensive Gardens。

gamma, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infr.en: This is the right list but from HIGH to low. The question asks low to high.
gamma, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infr.zh: 顺序对，但是从高到低。题目问的是从低到高。

radio, infrared, microwave, visible, X-r.en: Two pairs are swapped: microwave comes before infrared, and ultraviolet before X-ray.
radio, infrared, microwave, visible, X-r.zh: 有两对换了：微波在红外线前，紫外线在 X 光前。

microwave, radio, visible, infrared, ult.en: Radio is the lowest, so it comes first. Infrared comes before visible, and X-ray before gamma.
microwave, radio, visible, infrared, ult.zh: 无线电波最低，排第一。红外线在可见光前，X 光在伽马射线前。

questions.qzh: 从低频到高频，哪个顺序是对的？

ozh.radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ult: 无线电波、微波、红外线、可见光、紫外线、X 光、伽马射线
ozh.gamma, X-ray, ultraviolet, visible, infr: 伽马射线、X 光、紫外线、可见光、红外线、微波、无线电波
ozh.radio, infrared, microwave, visible, X-r: 无线电波、红外线、微波、可见光、X 光、紫外线、伽马射线
ozh.microwave, radio, visible, infrared, ult: 微波、无线电波、可见光、红外线、紫外线、伽马射线、X 光

questions.q: A TV remote control and a thermal camera both use...

why.en: Infrared is linked to heat and used in thermal imaging and remote controls.
why.zh: 红外线和热有关，用于热成像和遥控器。

ultraviolet.en: Ultraviolet causes sunburn and is used for security marks.
ultraviolet.zh: 紫外线会晒伤，用于防伪标记。

gamma rays.en: Gamma rays treat cancer; they would be dangerous in a TV remote.
gamma rays.zh: 伽马射线用于治疗癌症，用在遥控器里会很危险。

X-rays.en: X-rays are for medical images of bones.
X-rays.zh: X 光用于拍骨头的医学影像。

questions.qzh: 电视遥控器和热成像相机都用……

questions.q: Which EM wave is used to cook food and for radar?

why.en: Microwaves: cooking, radar and satellite communication.
why.zh: 微波：烹饪、雷达和卫星通信。

radio wave.en: Radio waves carry radio and TV broadcasts, not cooking.
radio wave.zh: 无线电波传送广播电视，不是做饭。

visible light.en: Visible light lets us see; it does not cook food in a microwave oven.
visible light.zh: 可见光让我们看见，不能在微波炉里做饭。

gamma ray.en: Gamma rays are too dangerous for cooking; they are used to kill cancer cells.
gamma ray.zh: 伽马射线太危险，不能做饭，用来杀癌细胞。

questions.qzh: 哪种电磁波用来做饭和做雷达？

questions.q: Too much sun can burn your skin. This is caused by...

why.en: UV has a higher frequency than visible light and can cause sunburn.
why.zh: 紫外线频率比可见光高，会晒伤皮肤。

infrared.en: Infrared is felt as HEAT (warmth from a fire). It is lower energy than visible light and does not burn skin cells like UV.
infrared.zh: 红外线让人感到热（火的温暖），能量比可见光低，不会像紫外线那样伤害皮肤细胞。

radio waves.en: Radio waves have very low energy and pass through us harmlessly.
radio waves.zh: 无线电波能量很低，穿过我们的身体也没有害处。

visible light.en: Visible light lets us see. Sunburn comes from the UV just beyond violet.
visible light.zh: 可见光让我们看见东西。晒伤来自紫光外面的紫外线。

questions.qzh: 晒太阳太多会晒伤皮肤。这是由……造成的。

questions.q: X-rays can make pictures of bones because they...
options: are seen by the human eye

why.en: X-rays pass through soft tissue, so medical images show the bones.
why.zh: X 射线能穿过软组织，所以医学影像能看到骨头。

are seen by the human eye.en: We cannot see X-rays. The image is made on a detector or film.
are seen by the human eye.zh: 我们看不见 X 光，影像是在探测器或胶片上形成的。

are low-frequency waves.en: X-rays are HIGH frequency, near the top of the spectrum.
are low-frequency waves.zh: X 光是高频的，在波谱的高端附近。

need a medium to travel.en: X-rays are EM waves, so they need no medium.
need a medium to travel.zh: X 光是电磁波，不需要介质。

questions.qzh: X 光能拍到骨头的照片，因为它们……

questions.q: Ionising radiation is dangerous because it...
options: removes electrons from atoms and can damage cells and DNA

why.en: It has enough energy to remove electrons from atoms, which can damage cells and DNA.
why.zh: 它的能量足以从原子中移走电子，会伤害细胞和 DNA。

is too quiet to hear.en: Radiation is not sound at all. Its danger is energy hitting cells.
is too quiet to hear.zh: 辐射根本不是声音，危险在于能量打到细胞上。

cannot travel through a vacuum.en: All EM waves CAN cross a vacuum. That is not the danger.
cannot travel through a vacuum.zh: 所有电磁波都能穿过真空，这不是危险所在。

is always visible.en: Ionising radiation (UV, X-ray, gamma) is INVISIBLE, which makes it more dangerous.
is always visible.zh: 电离辐射（紫外线、X 光、伽马射线）是看不见的，所以更危险。

questions.qzh: 电离辐射很危险，因为它……

ozh.removes electrons from atoms and can dam: 能把电子从原子里打出来，会伤害细胞和 DNA

canNow.en: I can now name the EM waves in order and give a use for each.
canNow.zh: 我现在能按顺序说出各种电磁波，并说出每种的用途。

title.en: Thursday Homework: Light, Colour and EM (B4 to B8)
title.zh: 星期四作业：光、颜色和电磁波（B4 到 B8）

subtitle.en: 12 questions, try as often as you like

intro.en: Read Main Book B4 to B8 first. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 先读主课本 B4 到 B8。可以做很多次。

questions.q: Frosted glass lets light through but you cannot see clearly through it. It is...

why.en: Translucent = light passes through but scatters.
why.zh: 半透明 = 光能通过但会散开。

transparent.en: Transparent means you can see clearly through it. Frosted glass is blurry on purpose.
transparent.zh: 透明是能清楚看过去。磨砂玻璃故意做成模糊的。

opaque.en: Opaque blocks ALL light, but frosted glass still lets light into the bathroom.
opaque.zh: 不透明会挡住所有光，但磨砂玻璃还是让光进到浴室。

luminous.en: Luminous means it makes its own light. Glass does not.
luminous.zh: 发光是自己发光，玻璃不会。

questions.qzh: 磨砂玻璃能透光，但看不清楚后面。它是……

questions.q: The Sun is...

why.en: The Sun produces its own light.
why.zh: 太阳自己发光。

non-luminous.en: Non-luminous objects only REFLECT light. The Sun makes its own light by nuclear reactions.
non-luminous.zh: 不发光的物体只反射光。太阳靠核反应自己发光。

opaque.en: Opaque is about blocking light that passes through. The question is whether it makes light.
opaque.zh: 不透明讲的是挡住穿过的光。题目问的是它会不会发光。

laterally inverted.en: Laterally inverted describes a mirror image, not the Sun.
laterally inverted.zh: 左右颠倒描述的是镜像，不是太阳。

questions.qzh: 太阳是……

questions.q: The normal is a line drawn at ___ to the surface.

why.en: The normal is an imaginary line at 90° to the surface.
why.zh: 法线是和表面成 90° 的假想线。

45°.en: 45° is halfway. The normal is always at a RIGHT angle (90°) to the surface.
45°.zh: 45° 只是一半。法线总是和表面成直角（90°）。

180°.en: 180° is a straight line, which would lie flat along the surface again.
180°.zh: 180° 是一条直线，又躺回表面上了。

0°.en: 0° would lie flat along the surface. The normal stands straight up at 90°.
0°.zh: 0° 是平躺在表面上。法线是 90° 竖起来的。

questions.qzh: 法线是和表面成 ___ 的线。

questions.q: The angle of incidence is 35°. The angle of reflection is...

why.en: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
why.zh: 入射角 = 反射角。

55°.en: 55° is 90° − 35°, the angle from the mirror surface. Both angles are measured from the normal, so they are equal.
55°.zh: 55° 是 90° − 35°，是从镜面量的角。两个角都从法线量，所以相等。

70°.en: 70° is 35° + 35°, the whole angle between the two rays. Each ray alone makes 35° with the normal.
70°.zh: 70° 是 35° + 35°，是两条光线之间的总角度。每条光线和法线各成 35°。

145°.en: 145° is 180° − 35°. The law of reflection says the two angles are EQUAL.
145°.zh: 145° 是 180° − 35°。反射定律说两个角相等。

questions.qzh: 入射角是 35°。反射角是……

questions.q: Writing looks back to front in a plane mirror. The image is...

why.en: A plane mirror reflects each point straight back, so left and right swap over: the image is laterally inverted (lateral = side). That is why AMBULANCE is written backwards on the front of ambulances.
why.zh: 平面镜把每个点直直反射回来，所以左右对调：像是左右颠倒的（lateral = 侧面）。所以救护车前面的 AMBULANCE 是反着写的。

refracted.en: Refraction is light bending as it passes INTO a new material, not bouncing off a mirror.
refracted.zh: 折射是光进入新物质时弯折，不是从镜子上反弹。

dispersed.en: Dispersion is white light splitting into colours.

absorbed.en: If the light were absorbed, you would see no image at all.
absorbed.zh: 如果光被吸收了，就根本看不到像。

questions.qzh: 在平面镜里，字看起来是反的。这个像是……

questions.q: Light bends when it goes from air into glass because its ___ changes.

why.en: Light travels at different speeds in different materials (fastest in air, slower in glass or water). When it enters a new material at an angle, the change in SPEED makes it change direction: refraction.
why.zh: 光在不同物质中速度不同（空气中最快，玻璃和水中较慢）。斜着进入新物质时，速度改变让它改变方向：折射。

colour.en: The colour stays the same when light enters a new material.
colour.zh: 光进入新物质时颜色不变。

amplitude.en: Amplitude is about brightness and does not bend light.
amplitude.zh: 振幅关系到亮度，不会让光弯折。

source.en: The source stays the same. The new MATERIAL changes the speed.
source.zh: 光源没变，是新的物质改变了速度。

questions.qzh: 光从空气进入玻璃时会弯折，因为它的 ___ 变了。

questions.q: A prism splits white light into colours. This is...

why.en: Dispersion = separating white light into its colours.
why.zh: 色散 = 把白光分成各种颜色。

reflection.en: Reflection bounces light back; it does not separate the colours.
reflection.zh: 反射把光弹回来，不会把颜色分开。

lateral inversion.en: Lateral inversion is a mirror swapping left and right.
lateral inversion.zh: 左右颠倒是镜子把左右换过来。

absorption.en: Absorption takes light in. A prism lets the light through and spreads it out.
absorption.zh: 吸收是把光吸进去。棱镜是让光通过并分散开。

questions.qzh: 棱镜把白光分成各种颜色。这是……

questions.q: Red light + green light = ?

why.en: Adding coloured LIGHT: red + green = yellow, red + blue = magenta, green + blue = cyan, and all three = white.
why.zh: 光的颜色相加：红 + 绿 = 黄，红 + 蓝 = 品红，绿 + 蓝 = 青，三种都加 = 白。

white.en: White needs all THREE primaries: red + green + blue.
white.zh: 白光要三种原色都有：红 + 绿 + 蓝。

questions.qzh: 红光 + 绿光 = ？

questions.q: A green leaf looks green because it...
options: reflects green light and absorbs the other colours

why.en: Objects reflect their own colour and absorb the rest.
why.zh: 物体反射自己的颜色，吸收其他颜色。

absorbs green light.en: If it absorbed green, no green would reach your eyes. We see the colour that is REFLECTED.
absorbs green light.zh: 如果吸收了绿光，就没有绿光进入眼睛。我们看到的是被反射的颜色。

makes its own green light.en: A leaf is non-luminous; it does not glow in the dark.
makes its own green light.zh: 叶子不发光，在黑暗里不会亮。

reflects all colours.en: Reflecting all colours makes something look WHITE.
reflects all colours.zh: 反射所有颜色的东西看起来是白的。

questions.qzh: 绿叶看起来是绿色的，因为它……

ozh.reflects green light and absorbs the oth: 反射绿光，吸收其他颜色

questions.q: Which EM wave can the human eye detect?

why.en: Visible light is the part of the EM spectrum the human eye can detect.
why.zh: 可见光是人眼能看到的那部分电磁波谱。

infrared.en: Infrared is just beyond red. We feel it as heat but cannot see it.
infrared.zh: 红外线在红光外面，我们能感到热，但看不见。

ultraviolet.en: Ultraviolet is just beyond violet. Our eyes cannot see it (some insects can).
ultraviolet.zh: 紫外线在紫光外面，我们的眼睛看不见（有些昆虫能）。

radio waves.en: Radio waves are invisible; we need a radio to detect them.
radio waves.zh: 无线电波看不见，要用收音机才能接收。

questions.qzh: 人眼能看见哪种电磁波？

questions.q: Which EM waves are used in cancer treatment?

why.en: Gamma rays: very high-frequency, used in cancer treatment.
why.zh: 伽马射线频率非常高，用于治疗癌症。

microwaves.en: Microwaves are for cooking, radar and phone signals.
microwaves.zh: 微波用于做饭、雷达和手机信号。

radio waves.en: Radio waves have very low energy and cannot destroy cancer cells.
radio waves.zh: 无线电波能量很低，不能摧毁癌细胞。

infrared.en: Infrared is heat radiation, used in remote controls and thermal cameras.
infrared.zh: 红外线是热辐射，用于遥控器和热成像。

questions.qzh: 治疗癌症用哪种电磁波？

questions.q: Which list is in order of INCREASING frequency?

why.en: Low to high frequency: radio, microwave, INFRARED, VISIBLE, ULTRAVIOLET, X-ray, gamma. Infrared is below red, ultraviolet is above violet, so the order is infrared, visible, ultraviolet.
why.zh: 从低频到高频：无线电波、微波、红外线、可见光、紫外线、X 光、伽马射线。红外线在红光下面，紫外线在紫光上面，所以顺序是红外线、可见光、紫外线。

ultraviolet, visible light, infrared.en: This is DECREASING frequency, the reverse.
ultraviolet, visible light, infrared.zh: 这是频率递减，反过来了。

visible light, infrared, ultraviolet.en: Infrared ("below red") is LOWER than visible light, so it comes first.
visible light, infrared, ultraviolet.zh: 红外线（“红光以下”）比可见光低，所以排第一。

ultraviolet, infrared, visible light.en: Ultraviolet is the HIGHEST of the three, so it must come last.
ultraviolet, infrared, visible light.zh: 紫外线是三个里最高的，所以要排最后。

questions.qzh: 哪一组是按频率从低到高排列的？

canNow.en: I can now explain light, colour and the EM spectrum.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释光、颜色和电磁波谱。

title.en: Friday Homework: Atoms to Word Equations (A1 to A5)
title.zh: 星期五作业：原子到文字方程式（A1 到 A5）

subtitle.en: 12 questions, try as often as you like

intro.en: Read Main Book A1 to A5 first. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 先读主课本 A1 到 A5。可以做很多次。

questions.q: A substance made of only ONE type of atom is...

why.en: An element is a pure substance made of only ONE type of atom, so it cannot be split into anything simpler. (Each box on the periodic table is one element.)
why.zh: 单质是只由一种原子组成的纯净物，不能再分成更简单的物质。（周期表上每一格是一种元素。）

a compound.en: A compound has two or more DIFFERENT types of atom joined.
a compound.zh: 化合物有两种或更多不同的原子结合。

a mixture.en: A mixture has two or more substances not joined.
a mixture.zh: 混合物是两种或更多物质没有结合。

an alloy.en: An alloy is a mixture of metals (like brass), so it has more than one type of atom.
an alloy.zh: 合金是金属的混合物（像黄铜），有不止一种原子。

questions.qzh: 只由一种原子组成的物质是……

questions.q: O₂ is...

why.en: O₂ is a molecule made of only oxygen atoms, so it is an element.
why.zh: O₂ 是只由氧原子组成的分子，所以是元素。

a compound.en: A compound needs two DIFFERENT elements. O₂ is only oxygen, just two atoms of it joined.
a compound.zh: 化合物需要两种不同元素。O₂ 只有氧，只是两个氧原子连在一起。

a mixture.en: A mixture has two or more substances. O₂ is one substance.
a mixture.zh: 混合物有两种或更多物质。O₂ 是一种物质。

a solution.en: A solution is something dissolved in a liquid, a kind of mixture.
a solution.zh: 溶液是东西溶在液体里，是混合物的一种。

questions.qzh: O₂ 是……

questions.q: Two or more elements chemically joined make a...

why.en: When two or more elements are CHEMICALLY joined, they make a new substance with a fixed formula and new properties: a compound.
why.zh: 两种或更多元素化学结合，就生成有固定化学式和新性质的新物质：化合物。

mixture.en: In a mixture the substances are NOT joined and can be separated easily.
mixture.zh: 混合物里的物质没有结合，容易分开。

solution.en: A solution is a mixture: something dissolved, not chemically joined.
solution.zh: 溶液是混合物：东西溶进去，没有化学结合。

pure element.en: An element has only ONE type of atom. Joining two elements gives something new.
pure element.zh: 单质只有一种原子。两种元素结合会变成新东西。

questions.qzh: 两种或更多元素化学结合形成……

questions.q: A particle diagram shows two kinds of particle, each made of only one kind of atom. This is a...

why.en: Two kinds of particle = mixture. Each particle one kind of atom = elements.
why.zh: 两种粒子 = 混合物。每个粒子只有一种原子 = 元素。

compound.en: In a compound the different atoms are JOINED in each particle. Here each particle has only one kind of atom.
compound.zh: 化合物的每个粒子里不同的原子是结合的。这里每个粒子只有一种原子。

mixture of two compounds.en: A compound particle has DIFFERENT atoms joined. These particles each have one kind of atom, so they are elements.
mixture of two compounds.zh: 化合物粒子里有不同的原子结合。这些粒子每个只有一种原子，所以是单质。

pure element.en: A pure element has only ONE kind of particle. Here there are two kinds.
pure element.zh: 纯单质只有一种粒子。这里有两种。

questions.qzh: 一张粒子图有两种粒子，每种都只由一种原子组成。这是……

questions.q: Co (capital C, small o) is...

why.en: One capital letter = one element. CO (two capitals) would be carbon monoxide.
why.zh: 一个大写字母 = 一种元素。CO（两个大写）才是一氧化碳。

carbon monoxide, a compound.en: Carbon monoxide is CO with TWO capital letters. Co has a small o, so it is one symbol.
carbon monoxide, a compound.zh: 一氧化碳是 CO，有两个大写字母。Co 的 o 是小写，是一个符号。

carbon and oxygen mixed.en: That would need C and O written as separate capitals. Co is one symbol: cobalt.
carbon and oxygen mixed.zh: 那要写成分开的大写 C 和 O。Co 是一个符号：钴。

copper.en: Copper's symbol is Cu (from its Latin name cuprum), not Co.
copper.zh: 铜的符号是 Cu（来自拉丁文 cuprum），不是 Co。

questions.qzh: Co（大写 C，小写 o）是……

questions.q: The symbol for iron is...

why.en: Iron's symbol is Fe, from its Latin name "ferrum". Some symbols come from old Latin names: Fe (iron), Cu (copper), Na (sodium), Au (gold).
why.zh: 铁的符号是 Fe，来自拉丁文 ferrum。有些符号来自古拉丁文：Fe（铁）、Cu（铜）、Na（钠）、Au（金）。

Ir.en: Ir is IRIDIUM, a different metal.
Ir.zh: Ir 是铱，是另一种金属。

In.en: In is INDIUM, a different metal.
In.zh: In 是铟，是另一种金属。

questions.qzh: 铁的符号是……

questions.q: How many atoms are in ONE molecule of H₂SO₄?

why.en: Add up every small number (no number means 1): H₂ = 2, S = 1, O₄ = 4. 2 + 1 + 4 = 7 atoms.
why.zh: 把所有小数字加起来（没写数字就是 1）：H₂ = 2，S = 1，O₄ = 4。2 + 1 + 4 = 7 个原子。

6.en: 6 forgets the S, which counts as 1 even though no number is written.
6.zh: 6 漏了 S，没写数字也算 1 个。

3.en: 3 counts the number of different ELEMENTS (H, S, O), not atoms.
3.zh: 3 是元素种类数（H、S、O），不是原子数。

questions.qzh: 一个 H₂SO₄ 分子里有几个原子？

questions.q: How many atoms are in 3 molecules of CO₂?

why.en: One CO₂ has 1 carbon + 2 oxygens = 3 atoms. Three molecules: 3 × 3 = 9 atoms.
why.zh: 一个 CO₂ 有 1 个碳 + 2 个氧 = 3 个原子。三个分子：3 × 3 = 9 个原子。

6.en: 6 is only the OXYGEN atoms (3 × 2). Add the 3 carbons too.
6.zh: 6 只是氧原子（3 × 2），还要加上 3 个碳。

5.en: 5 is 3 + 2, adding instead of multiplying. Each of the 3 molecules has 3 atoms.
5.zh: 5 是 3 + 2，加了而没有乘。3 个分子每个有 3 个原子。

3.en: 3 is the atoms in ONE molecule, or the number of molecules. There are 3 molecules of 3 atoms.
3.zh: 3 是一个分子的原子数，或者是分子数。这里是 3 个分子，每个 3 个原子。

questions.qzh: 3 个 CO₂ 分子里有几个原子？

questions.q: In H₂O, the ratio hydrogen : oxygen is...

why.en: H₂O = 2 hydrogens and 1 oxygen. Write the ratio in the order the question asks (hydrogen first): 2 : 1.
why.zh: H₂O = 2 个氢和 1 个氧。按题目顺序写比（氢在前）：2 : 1。

1 : 2.en: This is oxygen : hydrogen, the wrong order.
1 : 2.zh: 这是氧 : 氢，顺序反了。

2 : 2.en: There is only 1 oxygen in H₂O (no number after O means 1).
2 : 2.zh: H₂O 只有 1 个氧（O 后面没写数字就是 1）。

1 : 1.en: The small 2 after H means two hydrogens.
1 : 1.zh: H 后面的小 2 表示两个氢。

questions.qzh: 在 H₂O 里，氢 : 氧的比是……

questions.q: In iron + sulfur → iron sulfide, the reactants are...

why.en: Reactants are what you start with, on the left.
why.zh: 反应物是开始时的物质，在左边。

iron sulfide.en: Iron sulfide is the PRODUCT, on the right of the arrow.
iron sulfide.zh: 硫化亚铁是生成物，在箭头右边。

sulfur only.en: Both substances on the left are reactants: iron AND sulfur.
sulfur only.zh: 左边的两种物质都是反应物：铁和硫。

iron sulfide and iron.en: Iron sulfide is made, not started with, so it is not a reactant.
iron sulfide and iron.zh: 硫化亚铁是生成的，不是开始就有的，所以不是反应物。

questions.qzh: 在“铁 + 硫 → 硫化亚铁”里，反应物是……

questions.q: Sodium + chlorine → ?

why.en: Metal + non-metal: keep the metal name first and change the non-metal ending to -IDE. Chlorine → chloride, so sodium chloride (table salt).
why.zh: 金属 + 非金属：金属名称在前不变，非金属词尾改成 -ide。chlorine → chloride，所以是 sodium chloride（食盐）。

sodium chlorine.en: The non-metal must change its ending: chlorine → chloride.

chlorine sodide.en: The METAL comes first and keeps its name; only the non-metal gets -ide.
chlorine sodide.zh: 金属在前、名称不变；只有非金属加 -ide。

sodium chlorate.en: -ate means oxygen is also in it. Only sodium and chlorine reacted, so -ide.
sodium chlorate.zh: -ate 表示里面还有氧。只有钠和氯反应，所以用 -ide。

questions.qzh: 钠 + 氯 → ?（选正确的英文名称）

questions.q: SO₂ is called...

why.en: Name the first element, then the second with -ide, and add a prefix to count the atoms: mono = 1, di = 2, tri = 3. SO₂ has 2 oxygens, so sulfur DIoxide.
why.zh: 先写第一种元素，第二种改成 -ide，再加前缀表示原子数：mono = 1，di = 2，tri = 3。SO₂ 有 2 个氧，所以是 sulfur dioxide（二氧化硫）。

sulfur monoxide.en: Mono = 1. SO₂ has TWO oxygens, so di-.
sulfur monoxide.zh: mono = 1。SO₂ 有两个氧，所以用 di-。

sulfur oxide.en: This does not say HOW MANY oxygens. The small 2 needs the prefix di-.
sulfur oxide.zh: 这没说有几个氧。小的 2 要用前缀 di-。

sulfide dioxide.en: The FIRST element keeps its normal name (sulfur). Only the second gets -ide.
sulfide dioxide.zh: 第一种元素用原名（sulfur），只有第二种加 -ide。

questions.qzh: SO₂ 叫……（选正确的英文名称）

canNow.en: I can now explain atoms, compounds, formulae and word equations.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释原子、化合物、化学式和文字方程式。

title.en: Saturday Homework: Changes, States and Investigations (A6 to A8)
title.zh: 星期六作业：变化、物态和实验（A6 到 A8）

intro.en: Read Main Book A6 to A8 first. You can try again as many times as you like.
intro.zh: 先读主课本 A6 到 A8。可以做很多次。

questions.q: Which is a chemical change?

why.en: A chemical change makes a NEW substance and cannot easily be reversed. Burning paper makes ash, smoke and gases, and you cannot turn them back into paper.
why.zh: 化学变化产生新物质，不容易逆转。烧纸会产生灰、烟和气体，没法变回纸。

ice melting.en: Melting is a change of STATE. It is still water and can freeze again: physical.
ice melting.zh: 熔化是状态变化，还是水，可以再冻起来：物理变化。

sugar dissolving.en: The sugar is still there (the water tastes sweet) and you can get it back by evaporating: physical.
sugar dissolving.zh: 糖还在（水是甜的），蒸发后可以拿回来：物理变化。

water boiling.en: Boiling is a change of STATE: steam is still water and can condense back.
water boiling.zh: 沸腾是状态变化：水蒸气还是水，可以凝结回来。

questions.qzh: 哪个是化学变化？

questions.q: Bubbles of a new gas appear when two liquids are mixed. This is a sign of a...

why.en: A new gas appearing means a NEW substance was made, which is the sign of a chemical change. (Other signs: colour change, heat or light given out, a new solid.)
why.zh: 出现新的气体表示生成了新物质，这是化学变化的标志。（其他标志：颜色变化、放热或发光、生成新固体。）

physical change.en: A physical change makes no new substance. New gas bubbles mean something new was made.
physical change.zh: 物理变化不产生新物质。新的气泡表示有新东西生成。

melting point.en: Melting point is a temperature, not a sign of a reaction.
melting point.zh: 熔点是一个温度，不是反应的标志。

fair test.en: A fair test is a way of planning an experiment, not something you observe.
fair test.zh: 公平测试是设计实验的方法，不是观察到的现象。

questions.qzh: 两种液体混合时冒出了新气体的气泡。这是……的标志。

questions.q: 2.0 g of iron reacts with 0.8 g of sulfur. The mass of iron sulfide made is...

why.en: Conservation of mass: no atoms are lost or made, so all the iron and all the sulfur end up in the product. 2.0 g + 0.8 g = 2.8 g.
why.zh: 质量守恒：原子不会消失也不会产生，所以所有的铁和硫都在生成物里。2.0 g + 0.8 g = 2.8 g。

1.2 g.en: 1.2 g is 2.0 − 0.8: subtracting. The sulfur JOINS the iron, so the masses add.
1.2 g.zh: 1.2 g 是 2.0 − 0.8，减了。硫是加到铁上的，所以质量相加。

2.0 g.en: 2.0 g is only the iron. The 0.8 g of sulfur joined it, so the mass goes up.
2.0 g.zh: 2.0 g 只是铁。0.8 g 的硫结合上去了，质量会增加。

1.6 g.en: 1.6 g is 0.8 × 2. The masses of the reactants simply add up.
1.6 g.zh: 1.6 g 是 0.8 × 2。反应物的质量只是相加。

questions.qzh: 2.0 g 铁和 0.8 g 硫反应。生成的硫化亚铁质量是……

questions.q: In a liquid, the particles are...
options: touching but random, and they slide

why.en: Solid = neat rows. Liquid = touching, random, sliding. Gas = far apart.
why.zh: 固体 = 整齐排列。液体 = 挨着、随机、滑动。气体 = 离得很远。

in neat rows, only wiggling.en: Neat rows that only vibrate describes a SOLID.
in neat rows, only wiggling.zh: 整齐排列、只能振动的是固体。

far apart and moving fast.en: Far apart and fast describes a GAS.
far apart and moving fast.zh: 离得远、运动快的是气体。

not moving at all.en: Particles are ALWAYS moving, even in a solid (they vibrate).
not moving at all.zh: 粒子一直在运动，就算在固体里也在振动。

questions.qzh: 在液体里，粒子……

ozh.touching but random, and they slide: 互相接触但杂乱，能滑动

questions.q: Gas turning into a liquid is called...

why.en: Gas → liquid = condensing.
why.zh: 气体 → 液体 = 冷凝。

boiling.en: Boiling is liquid → gas, the opposite.
boiling.zh: 沸腾是液体 → 气体，正相反。

questions.qzh: 气体变成液体叫……

questions.q: Mercury melts at -39 °C and boils at 357 °C. At 20 °C, mercury is a...

why.en: 20 is hotter than -39 but colder than 357, so it is between: liquid.
why.zh: 20 比 -39 热，比 357 冷，在两者之间：液体。

solid.en: Mercury is only solid BELOW −39 °C. 20 °C is warmer than that, so it has melted.
solid.zh: 汞只有低于 −39 °C 才是固体。20 °C 比这暖，已经熔化了。

gas.en: Mercury only becomes a gas above 357 °C. 20 °C is far below that.
gas.zh: 汞要高于 357 °C 才变成气体。20 °C 远低于此。

mixture.en: Mercury is an element (Hg). The question asks about its STATE.
mixture.zh: 汞是单质（Hg）。题目问的是状态。

questions.qzh: 汞在 -39 °C 熔化，在 357 °C 沸腾。在 20 °C 时汞是……

questions.q: Which temperature is the coldest?

why.en: On a number line, the further LEFT a number is, the smaller (colder) it is. −40 is furthest left: −40 < −5 < 0 < 12.
why.zh: 数轴上越往左越小（越冷）。−40 在最左边：−40 < −5 < 0 < 12。

-5 °C.en: −5 °C is below freezing, but −40 is 35 degrees colder.
-5 °C.zh: −5 °C 低于冰点，但 −40 °C 还要冷 35 度。

0 °C.en: 0 °C is warmer than any negative temperature.

12 °C.en: 12 °C is above zero, the warmest here.
12 °C.zh: 12 °C 在零度以上，是这里最暖的。

questions.qzh: 哪个温度最冷？

questions.q: Emma tests how the water temperature changes the time for sugar to dissolve. The independent variable is the...

why.en: The independent variable is the ONE thing you choose to change on purpose. Emma changes the water TEMPERATURE to see what happens.
why.zh: 自变量是你故意改变的那一样。Emma 改变的是水的温度，看会发生什么。

time to dissolve.en: The time is what she MEASURES: the dependent variable.
time to dissolve.zh: 时间是她测量的：因变量。

mass of sugar.en: The mass of sugar must stay the SAME to keep it fair: a control variable.
mass of sugar.zh: 糖的质量要保持不变才公平：控制变量。

volume of water.en: The volume of water must stay the same too: a control variable.
volume of water.zh: 水的体积也要保持不变：控制变量。

questions.qzh: Emma 测试水温怎样影响糖溶解的时间。自变量是……

questions.q: In a results table, the first column shows...

why.en: The first column of a results table is always the independent variable, what you CHANGE, with its unit in the heading. The measurements go in the columns after it.
why.zh: 结果表的第一列永远是自变量（你改变的东西），表头写单位。测量结果放在后面的列。

what you keep the same.en: Control variables stay the same, so they do not need a column; you state them in the method.
what you keep the same.zh: 控制变量保持不变，不需要一列，在方法里写明就行。

your name.en: A name is not data. Tables only hold variables.
your name.zh: 名字不是数据，表格只放变量。

the conclusion.en: The conclusion is written in sentences AFTER the table, not in it.
the conclusion.zh: 结论是在表格后面用句子写的，不在表格里。

questions.qzh: 在结果表里，第一列是……

questions.q: A magnet is moved over iron sulfide (after heating iron and sulfur). What happens?
options: the magnet cannot pull the iron out
the iron sticks to the magnet
the sulfur sticks to the magnet
it turns back into iron and sulfur

why.en: Iron sulfide is a compound: the iron is chemically joined.
why.zh: 硫化亚铁是化合物：铁已经化学结合了。

the iron sticks to the magnet.en: In iron sulfide the iron is chemically joined to sulfur. The new compound is not magnetic.
the iron sticks to the magnet.zh: 硫化亚铁里的铁和硫化学结合了，新的化合物没有磁性。

the sulfur sticks to the magnet.en: Sulfur is never magnetic, joined or not.
the sulfur sticks to the magnet.zh: 硫从来没有磁性，结合与否都一样。

it turns back into iron and sulfur.en: A magnet cannot undo a chemical reaction. Separating a compound needs another chemical reaction.
it turns back into iron and sulfur.zh: 磁铁不能逆转化学反应。分开化合物需要另一个化学反应。

questions.qzh: 把磁铁移到硫化亚铁上面（铁和硫加热之后）。会发生什么？

questions.q: Which is a PHYSICAL change?

why.en: A physical change makes NO new substance and can be reversed. Melted ice is still water and can be frozen again.
why.zh: 物理变化不产生新物质，可以逆转。融化的冰还是水，可以再冻起来。

paper burning.en: Burning makes new substances (ash, smoke, gases): chemical.
paper burning.zh: 燃烧产生新物质（灰、烟、气体）：化学变化。

iron rusting.en: Rust (iron oxide) is a new substance made when iron joins with oxygen: chemical.
iron rusting.zh: 铁锈（氧化铁）是铁和氧结合产生的新物质：化学变化。

an egg cooking.en: Cooking changes the egg's proteins for good and cannot be undone: chemical.
an egg cooking.zh: 煮熟会永久改变蛋白质，不能逆转：化学变化。

questions.qzh: 哪个是物理变化？

questions.q: The mass of a metal goes UP after heating in air. Who was right?

why.en: Lavoisier said a heated metal JOINS with oxygen from the air. Gaining oxygen atoms adds mass, so the mass goes up, which is what happened.
why.zh: 拉瓦锡说金属加热时会和空气中的氧结合。多了氧原子质量就增加，结果正是这样。

Priestley.en: Priestley's idea (phlogiston) said metals LOSE something when heated, so the mass should go DOWN. It went up.
Priestley.zh: 普里斯特利的理论（燃素）说金属加热会失去东西，质量应该下降。结果质量上升了。

both.en: Their ideas predict opposite results (mass up vs mass down), so the evidence cannot support both.
both.zh: 他们的理论预测相反的结果（质量上升和下降），证据不可能同时支持两个人。

neither.en: The mass going up fits Lavoisier's idea: the metal joined with oxygen from the air.
neither.zh: 质量上升符合拉瓦锡的理论：金属和空气中的氧结合了。

questions.qzh: 金属在空气中加热后质量增加了。谁是对的？

canNow.en: I can now explain changes, states of matter and fair tests.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释物质变化、物态和公平测试。

title.zh: 1. 练习：光的词汇（B4 到 B7）

intro.en: Read the keyword, say the meaning in your own words, then tap to check.
intro.zh: 读关键词，用自己的话说出意思，再点卡片检查。

cards.back: A material that allows light to pass through clearly, so objects can be seen through it.
cards.zhBack: 能让光清楚地通过的材料，可以看清后面的东西。

cards.back: A material that allows light through but scatters it, so objects cannot be seen clearly through it.
cards.zhBack: 能让光通过但会把光散开的材料，看不清后面的东西。

cards.back: A material that does not allow light to pass through it.
cards.zhBack: 不让光通过的材料。

cards.back: An object that produces its own light.
cards.zhBack: 自己能发光的物体。

cards.back: An object that does not produce its own light, but can be seen by light reflected off it.
cards.zhBack: 自己不发光，但能靠反射的光被看见的物体。

cards.back: A straight line used to show the direction in which light travels.
cards.zhBack: 表示光传播方向的直线。

cards.back: A flat mirror with a smooth, reflective surface.
cards.zhBack: 表面平滑、能反光的平的镜子。

cards.back: When an image appears reversed from left to right, as in a plane mirror.
cards.zhBack: 像的左右反过来，就像在平面镜里一样。

cards.back: The change in direction of light when it bounces off a surface.
cards.zhBack: 光碰到表面弹回来时方向的改变。

cards.back: The change in direction of light when it passes between different materials because its speed changes.
cards.zhBack: 光从一种材料进入另一种材料时，因为速度改变而改变方向。

cards.back: The ray of light travelling towards a surface before reflection or refraction.
cards.zhBack: 反射或折射之前，射向表面的光线。

cards.back: The ray of light that bounces off a surface.
cards.zhBack: 从表面弹回来的光线。

cards.back: The angle between the incident ray and the normal.
cards.zhBack: 入射光线和法线之间的夹角。

cards.back: The angle between the reflected ray and the normal.
cards.zhBack: 反射光线和法线之间的夹角。

cards.back: An imaginary line drawn at 90° to a surface at the point where a ray hits it.
cards.zhBack: 在光线射到表面的那一点，画一条和表面成 90° 的假想线。

cards.back: A transparent object, usually made of glass or plastic, that can refract and disperse light.
cards.zhBack: 通常用玻璃或塑料做的透明物体，能折射光并把光分散开。

cards.back: The separation of white light into its different colours.
cards.zhBack: 白光分成各种颜色。

cards.back: A range of different colours or wavelengths, such as the visible spectrum.
cards.zhBack: 一系列不同的颜色或波长，例如可见光谱。

cards.back: To allow something, such as light, to pass through a material.
cards.zhBack: 让光等东西穿过一种材料。

cards.back: To take in energy, such as light, rather than reflecting or transmitting it.
cards.zhBack: 把光等能量吸进去，而不是反射或透射。

cards.back: A colour of light that can be combined with other primary colours to produce a range of colours. For light, these are red, green and blue.
cards.zhBack: 能和其他原色混合出很多颜色的色光。光的三原色是红、绿、蓝。

cards.back: A colour produced by mixing two primary colours of light. These are cyan, magenta and yellow.
cards.zhBack: 两种原色光混合得到的颜色：青色、品红色和黄色。

canNow.en: I can now explain the 22 light keywords.
canNow.zh: 我现在能解释 22 个关于光的关键词。

intro.en: The big rule: angle of incidence = angle of reflection, both measured from the normal.
intro.zh: 最重要的规则：入射角 = 反射角，都从法线量起。

questions.q: Window glass is...

why.en: Light passes clearly: transparent.
why.zh: 光清楚地通过：透明。

translucent.en: Translucent glass (frosted) is blurry. You can see clearly through a window, so it is transparent.
translucent.zh: 半透明玻璃（磨砂）看不清。窗户能看清楚，所以是透明的。

opaque.en: Opaque blocks all light. Light comes through a window.
opaque.zh: 不透明会挡住所有光。窗户是透光的。

luminous.en: Luminous means it makes its own light. Glass does not.
luminous.zh: 发光是自己发光，玻璃不会。

questions.qzh: 窗户玻璃是……

questions.q: Frosted bathroom glass is...

why.en: Light passes but scatters: translucent.
why.zh: 光能通过但会散开：半透明。

transparent.en: Transparent means you can see clearly through it. Frosted glass is blurry on purpose.
transparent.zh: 透明是能清楚看过去。磨砂玻璃故意做成模糊的。

opaque.en: Opaque blocks ALL light, but frosted glass still lets light into the bathroom.
opaque.zh: 不透明会挡住所有光，但磨砂玻璃还是让光进到浴室。

non-luminous only.en: It is non-luminous, but that only says it makes no light. The question is how light passes through.
non-luminous only.zh: 它确实不发光，但那只说明它自己不发光。题目问的是光怎样穿过。

questions.qzh: 浴室的磨砂玻璃是……

questions.q: A wooden door is...

why.en: No light passes: opaque.
why.zh: 光不能通过：不透明。

transparent.en: You cannot see through a wooden door, so it is not transparent.
transparent.zh: 木门看不过去，所以不透明。

translucent.en: Translucent lets some light through. A wooden door lets none.
translucent.zh: 半透明会透一些光。木门一点都不透。

luminous.en: A door makes no light of its own.

questions.qzh: 木门是……

questions.q: Which is LUMINOUS?

why.en: It makes its own light.
why.zh: 它自己发光。

the Moon.en: The Moon only REFLECTS sunlight, so it is non-luminous.
the Moon.zh: 月亮只是反射阳光，所以不是光源。

a mirror.en: A mirror only reflects light from other things.
a mirror.zh: 镜子只反射别的东西的光。

a white wall.en: A white wall reflects a lot of light but makes none itself.
a white wall.zh: 白墙反射很多光，但自己不发光。

questions.qzh: 哪个会自己发光？

questions.q: We see a book because...
options: light reflects off it into our eyes

why.en: Non-luminous objects are seen by reflected light.
why.zh: 不发光的物体靠反射光被看见。

it makes its own light.en: A book is non-luminous: in a dark room you cannot see it.
it makes its own light.zh: 书不发光：在黑屋子里你看不到它。

our eyes send out light.en: Eyes RECEIVE light; they do not send it out. That is why we cannot see in the dark.
our eyes send out light.zh: 眼睛是接收光，不是发出光。所以在黑暗中看不见。

it is opaque.en: Being opaque only means light cannot pass through it. We see it because light BOUNCES off it into our eyes.
it is opaque.zh: 不透明只表示光穿不过去。我们看到它是因为光从它上面反射进眼睛。

questions.qzh: 我们能看到书，是因为……

ozh.light reflects off it into our eyes: 光从它上面反射进我们的眼睛

questions.q: Light rays are drawn as...

why.en: Light travels in straight lines. The arrow shows the direction.
why.zh: 光沿直线传播，箭头表示方向。

wavy lines.en: Light is a wave, but a ray shows the PATH it travels, which is straight.
wavy lines.zh: 光是波，但光线表示的是它走的路线，是直的。

circles.en: Circles do not show a direction of travel.
circles.zh: 圆圈不能表示传播方向。

dotted curves.en: Light does not curve in air. Dotted lines are only used for the normal or for virtual rays behind a mirror.
dotted curves.zh: 光在空气中不会弯。虚线只用来画法线或镜子后面的虚像光线。

questions.qzh: 光线画成……

questions.q: The angle of incidence is 30°. The angle of reflection is...

why.en: Law of reflection: the angle of incidence EQUALS the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal. 30° in, 30° out.
why.zh: 反射定律：入射角等于反射角，都从法线量。入射 30°，反射也是 30°。

60°.en: 60° is 90° − 30°, the angle from the mirror surface. Angles are measured from the normal, so it stays 30°.
60°.zh: 60° 是 90° − 30°，是从镜面量的。角要从法线量，所以还是 30°。

90°.en: 90° is the angle between the normal and the mirror.
90°.zh: 90° 是法线和镜面之间的角。

150°.en: 150° is 180° − 30°. The law says the two angles are equal.

questions.qzh: 入射角是 30°。反射角是……

questions.q: Angles in a ray diagram are measured from the...

why.en: The normal is a line at 90° to the surface where the ray hits. All angles in ray diagrams are measured from it, so the law of reflection works on any surface.
why.zh: 法线是在光线射到的地方和表面成 90° 的线。光路图里所有角都从它量，这样反射定律在任何表面都适用。

mirror surface.en: Measuring from the mirror gives the wrong angle (90° minus the real one).
mirror surface.zh: 从镜面量会得到错误的角（90° 减去真正的角）。

top of the page.en: The page has nothing to do with the ray; the normal is drawn where the ray hits.
top of the page.zh: 纸的边和光线无关，法线画在光线射到的地方。

light source.en: The light source can be anywhere. Angles are measured at the mirror, from the normal.
light source.zh: 光源可以在任何地方。角是在镜面上从法线量的。

questions.qzh: 光路图里的角是从……量的。

questions.q: The ray that bounces OFF the mirror is the...

why.en: Incident = going in. Reflected = bouncing off.
why.zh: 入射 = 射进来；反射 = 弹出去。

incident ray.en: The incident ray is the one going IN, towards the mirror.
incident ray.zh: 入射光线是射向镜子的那条。

normal.en: The normal is the 90° construction line, not a ray of light.
normal.zh: 法线是画出来的 90° 辅助线，不是光线。

refracted ray.en: A refracted ray goes INTO a new material and bends, like into glass or water.
refracted ray.zh: 折射光线是进入新物质时弯折的光线，比如进入玻璃或水。

questions.qzh: 从镜子上反弹回来的光线叫……

questions.q: In a plane mirror, your right hand looks like a left hand. This is called...

why.en: Laterally inverted = reversed left to right.
why.zh: 左右颠倒 = 左右反过来。

refraction.en: Refraction is light bending as it enters a new material.
refraction.zh: 折射是光进入新物质时弯折。

dispersion.en: Dispersion is white light splitting into colours.
dispersion.zh: 色散是白光分成各种颜色。

absorption.en: Absorption is a material taking in light.
absorption.zh: 吸收是物质把光吸进去。

canNow.en: I can now sort materials and use the law of reflection.
canNow.zh: 我现在会给材料分类，并会用反射定律。
